kind: assumed or cited inputs; nothing in this file is measured in the Demerzel repository
random_seed_note: The analysis draws no random numbers: every result is an exact count or a ratio of counts.

horizon_bounds_days.note: Analysis choice, not an observation: a pair of feeder runs counts as 'about a day apart' when its gap lies inside these bounds.

synthetic_candidates.note: Imaginary forecasters scored on the observed label pairs. Each is defined only by how it would have behaved: how many of the observed label changes it called (change and new label both right), how many it missed, and how many times it announced a change that did not happen. None of them exists; the counts are assumptions.

echo.description: Any model, however elaborate, whose output equals the previous label on every pair.

one_false_alarm.description: Copies the previous label except for one announced change that did not happen.

one_right_call.description: Calls the one observed change and never announces another.

cautious_alarm.description: Calls the one observed change and also announces three changes that did not happen.

extrapolation.assumption: The share of pairs that change stays at the observed share and every future run has as many artifacts as the latest observed run. One observed change does not support this assumption; it only sets a scale.

cited_example.name: Finley's tornado forecasts, United States, 1884
cited_example.source: Contingency table as published by the WWRP/WGNE Joint Working Group on Forecast Verification Research (JWGFVR), 'Forecast verification - methods, issues and FAQ', section 'Finley tornado forecasts'; history in Murphy (1996), 'The Finley Affair: A Signal Event in the History of Forecast Verification', Weather and Forecasting 11, 3-20.

transfer_task.note: Hypothetical runbook registry for the learner task. Not Streeling data and not a forecast.
